claim: TER one-way fares from Nice-Ville: Villefranche €2.10 (5 min), Monaco €4.40 (20 min), Antibes €5.20 (25 min), Cannes €7.90 (40 min); trains run roughly every 15 minutes until ~10pm
quote: Villefranche-sur-mer: €2.10 (5 min); Monaco: €4.40 (20 min); Antibes: €5.20 (25 min); Cannes: €7.90 (40 min)... Trains run roughly every 15 minutes in both directions until around 10pm

claim: TER trains link Cannes to Ventimiglia along the coast, calling at all main Côte d'Azur towns; Nice-Ville is the main station
quote: TER (Trains Express Régionaux) provide a fast link between Cannes and Ventimiglia for all the main towns along on the Côte d'Azur coast

claim: Lignes d'Azur 2026 fares: single €1.70 (74 min transfers), 10-trip card €15, 24-hour pass €7, 7-day pass €20, monthly €45
quote: Single ride: €1.70; 10-trip card: €15.00; 24-hour pass: €7.00; 7-day pass: €20.00; Monthly subscription: €45.00

claim: Tram T2 connects Nice Côte d'Azur Airport to central Nice in 20-30 minutes for €1.70, running every 7-8 minutes weekdays from ~5:30am to ~11:55pm
quote: Tram Line 2 connects NCE directly to central Nice in 20-30 minutes... A tram to the airport runs every 7 to 8 minutes on weekdays... from 5.30 AM to 11.55 PM

claim: Nice has three tram lines: T1 (Henri Sappia–Hôpital Pasteur via Masséna/Garibaldi), T2 (airport to Port Lympia), T3 (airport to Saint-Isidore)
quote: Line T1 runs from Henri Sappia to Hôpital Pasteur... Line T2 connects the airport (Terminals 1 and 2) to the city center and Port Lympia... Line T3 primarily serves the western part of the city

claim: Bus #82 from Vauban serves Èze Village (the perched village); #602 alternates with it, about once an hour, ~30 min, €1.70; bus #600 only reaches Èze-sur-Mer at sea level
quote: Bus #82 (Plateau de la Justice) or Bus #602 (Monaco Casino)... approximately once per hour... Cost: With rechargeable Nice card: €1.70... Avoid Bus #600 (Monaco), which goes to Eze-sur-Mer (seaside) rather than Eze Village

claim: Bus #600 (which absorbed the old #100, #607 and #608 in April 2024) runs Nice-Villefranche-Beaulieu-Èze-sur-Mer-Cap-d'Ail-Monaco-Roquebrune-Menton every 15 min weekdays, 20 min Sundays; trip ~1 hour
quote: Since April 6, 2024, route 607... and route 608... merged to create route 600, the former route 100... The trip takes one hour, and the bus #600 leaves every 15 minutes during the week, and every 20 minutes on Sundays

claim: Bus #15 from Lycée Masséna runs to Villefranche-sur-Mer and Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat in ~15 minutes; takes the train back since #600 is often full returning from Monaco; service ends ~8-8:30pm
quote: Bus #15 Port de Saint-Jean - Departs from Lycee Massena bus stop... The journey takes approximately 15 minutes. Both buses run until around 8pm-8:30pm... Bus #600 is usually already full on its way back from Monaco

claim: Bus 5 (not 15) serves the Musée Matisse and Musée National Marc Chagall in the hillside Cimiez neighborhood; bus 82 serves Èze Village; bus 15 serves Villefranche, Beaulieu and St-Jean-Cap-Ferrat
quote: Bus 5 serves the Musée Matisse and Musée National Marc Chagall in the hillside neighbourhood of Cimiez, bus 82 goes to Èze Village, and bus 15 serves Villefranche-sur-Mer, Beaulieu-sur-Mer and St-Jean-Cap-Ferrat

claim: Nice in June: daytime ~24-27°C, nights ~17°C, sea ~23°C, ~12 hours of sunshine, rain rare; June is start of high season but markedly less crowded than July-August peak
quote: Expect 24°C (75°F) during the day and 17°C (63°F) at night... The sea temperature reaches 23°C... June has the most sunshine of the year in Nice with an average of 12 hours of sunshine... Nice in June is lively but not as crowded as the peak summer months of July and August

claim: The 2026 Monaco Grand Prix moves from its traditional late-May slot to June 5-7, 2026 — directly affecting weekend visitors to Nice/Monaco that weekend
quote: The 2026 Monaco Grand Prix takes place in early June, with practice starting on Friday June 5 and the race on Sunday June 7

claim: The 79th Cannes Film Festival ran 12-23 May 2026, with restricted access to the festival zone — a major crowd/price driver in May
quote: The 79th annual Cannes Film Festival took place from 12 to 23 May 2026... Access to the festival zone was restricted to festival-goers from 12 to 23 May, 2026

claim: Jazz à Juan in Juan-les-Pins runs 9-19 July 2026; Nice Jazz Festival runs 23-26 July 2026
quote: The Jazz à Juan Festival runs from 9 to 19 July 2026... The 2026 Nice Jazz Festival takes place 23 – 26 July 2026

claim: Nice Carnival 2026 ran 11 February-1 March with flower battles, illuminated parades and tickets €5-€28 (free in costume)
quote: The carnival kicks off on 11 February with the Grand Charivari and culminates on 28 February... prices from €5 to €28, and the Carnival is free if you attend in costume

claim: Vieux Nice (Old Town) hotels from ~$161/night; Carré d'Or is the central rectangle bounded by Ave Jean Médecin, Bd Victor Hugo, Bd Gambetta and the Promenade; Promenade des Anglais area runs ~17% below the city average of $143
quote: Vieux-Nice hotels have been found for as cheap as $161/night... Le Carré d'Or Area in the city centre covers a rectangular area of Ave Jean Medecin, Bd Victor Hugo, Bd Gambetta and the Promenade... Hotels near Promenade des Anglais are typically 17% less expensive than the average hotel in Nice

claim: Nice is generally safe; main risk is pickpocketing along Promenade des Anglais, in Old Town, at markets and on trams/trains, often by groups using ticket-machine distractions
quote: Pickpockets are very active on the trams/trains and in tourist areas. They operate in groups, usually offering to help you buy a ticket, to distract you and then take what they can

claim: The original Vélo Bleu municipal bike share has been replaced by Pony (blue, e-bikes) and Lime (green) free-floating fleets totalling ~2000 bikes, ~90% electric
quote: The original Velo Bleu system has been replaced by two new bike share fleets with 2000 bikes total, 90% of which are electric. The new blue bikes are operated by Pony... and the Day-Glo green bikes are operated by Lime
